title: Prove the odd-denominator mW call floor with arbitrary auxiliaries
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds a uniform rank-one call bound for the full address lattice `q^-1 M_m(Z)` with fixed odd `q`. If each cleared data target `q C_i mod 2` is invertible, then any word using `k` paid rank-one calls satisfies `k >= mW`, even with arbitrarily many dirty auxiliary registers and free interleaved `GL_n(F2)` mixing. The column decomposition gives a matching `mW`-call construction. The proof also covers the data-to-data endpoint condition when auxiliary output blocks are unconstrained.

For `m=W=3`, the package gives an exact nine-call word for `C1=I`, `C2=I+E21`, `C3=I+E32`. The new mechanism is a square-zero augmentation of the formal additive group algebra; each call contributes a matrix of rank at most one on register-address space, while the data block has rank nine. It permits arbitrary rational relations among frames. This is a scoped algebraic result, not a supplier implementation or a `kappa` improvement. Even-denominator frames and targets singular after clearing are outside the bound.

## Task and overlap

- Track/task: `bit-mechanisms` / `bit-new-register-model`; seed `16c9467a282673c96099aae5db2415a9`; priority revision 4; refined scope.
- Exact base: `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`; catalogue and predecessor pins are in `SOURCES.json`.
- This extends the arbitrary-register one-relation lemma to unrestricted relation rank under the odd-lattice hypothesis, and extends dirty-auxiliary coverage from two active roles to arbitrary `W`. PR #1974 uses the finite `F2[GL3(F2)]` label group, and PR #2027 uses `UT4(F2)`; neither is this rational additive lattice. Current S3/finite-GL3 claims (#2012 and #2102) use different address groups; the four-role rational-frame claim #2091 includes a half-integral frame and lies outside this odd-denominator premise.
- Original claim: [Discussion #1167 comment 18932466](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1167#discussioncomment-18932466).

## Validation

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/bit-odd-denominator-register-floor-seed16c946/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-odd-denominator-register-floor-seed16c946 --check-only
```

The exact formal replay passed on CPython 3.14.7. It checks the nine-call word with 0, 1, and 3 auxiliaries; source hashes; the rank-nine target block; odd-lattice additivity; rank-one projector and mixer controls; and deleted-call, mutated-frame, wrong-endpoint, even-determinant, and even-denominator controls. Package metadata and source pins pass. The registered replay requires Python 3.12, which is unavailable on this host, so the repository package runner was not executed locally; `--check-only` validates metadata and pins only.

The full favorable bill gives auxiliary storage and free scalar mixing at no charge; even then the minimum equals the direct construction. No recursive hosting, native implementation, precision, or selected-profile saving is claimed.

## Credit

Predecessor results and licenses are retained in `SOURCES.json`. Prepared for Cinna Davis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in the derivation, verifier, and writing. No subagents, independent human review, or proof-assistant formalization are claimed.

## Open next questions

Can even-denominator frames use auxiliary registers to beat `mW` calls for these same endpoints? Start with one dyadic denominator and two exact frame relations; derive the full dirty-input endpoint and bill before searching larger words. The blocker is that no exact dyadic saving candidate or invariant is known.
